column3: This is the word for the place where a person lives, as asked on forms and applications. 地址 is the general word for any address, such as a shop's or an email address.
column6: Qǐng xiě xià nǐ de zhùzhǐ.
column7: Please write down your address.
column9: This is the word for the place where a person lives, as asked on forms and applications. 地址 is the general word for any address, such as a shop's or an email address.

column3: Mother tongue, native language: 我的母语是英语. 母 is "mother" and 语 "language". For the language of a country or people, 语 is also the ending: 英语, 日语.
column7: My native language is English.
column9: Mother tongue, native language: 我的母語是英語. 母 is "mother" and 語 "language". For the language of a country or people, 語 is also the ending: 英語, 日語.

column3: A clock that hangs on a wall or stands on a table. A wristwatch is a 手表 and an alarm clock a 闹钟. 钟 alone means a large bell as well as a clock.
column6: Kètīng lǐ yǒu yī ge dà shízhōng.
column7: There is a big clock in the living room.
column9: A clock that hangs on a wall or stands on a table. A wristwatch is a 手錶 and an alarm clock a 鬧鐘. 鐘 alone means a large bell as well as a clock.

column3: A written, descriptive word for the time after dark: 夜晚很安静. In everyday speech people say 晚上, and 半夜 for the middle of the night.
column7: The seaside is quiet at night.
column9: A written, descriptive word for the time after dark: 夜晚很安靜. In everyday speech people say 晚上, and 半夜 for the middle of the night.

column3: Breakfast, especially the Chinese kind sold at breakfast stands, such as soy milk and 烧饼. The usual general word is 早餐. The same two characters also appear when 早 and 一点 mean "a bit earlier", as in 早点睡.
column7: We eat breakfast outside.
column9: Breakfast, especially the Chinese kind sold at breakfast stands, such as soy milk and 燒餅. The usual general word is 早餐. The same two characters also appear when 早 and 一點 mean "a bit earlier", as in 早點睡.

column3: A spoken word, and also how you address him. 外 marks the mother's side of the family, as in 外婆, while the father's father is 爷爷. In the north he is usually 姥爷.
column7: My maternal grandfather lives in Tainan.
column9: A spoken word, and also how you address him. 外 marks the mother's side of the family, as in 外婆, while the father's father is 爺爺. In the north he is usually 姥爺.

column3: The spoken word for your mother's mother, matching 外公. Your father's mother is 奶奶. In the north she is usually 姥姥.
column6: Wàipó zuò de cài hěn hǎochī.
column7: My grandmother's cooking is delicious.
column9: The spoken word for your mother's mother, matching 外公. Your father's mother is 奶奶. In the north she is usually 姥姥.

column3: Children also use it for an older man who is a friend of their father, often with his surname: 王伯伯. Your father's younger brother is 叔叔, so 伯 and 叔 tell you whether he is older or younger than your father.
column7: My uncle is coming to our house today.
column9: Children also use it for an older man who is a friend of their father, often with his surname: 王伯伯. Your father's younger brother is 叔叔, so 伯 and 叔 tell you whether he is older or younger than your father.

column3: Mostly met in compounds: 伯父 and 伯母 for an uncle and his wife, and 大伯 for the eldest of the father's brothers. It is the third rank of the old nobility too, in 伯爵 "count".
column7: Good morning, Uncle Wang!
column9: Mostly met in compounds: 伯父 and 伯母 for an uncle and his wife, and 大伯 for the eldest of the father's brothers. It is the third rank of the old nobility too, in 伯爵 "count".

column3: More formal than 伯伯. It is also a respectful way to talk about or address an older man who is a friend of your father: 李伯父. The wife is 伯母.
column7: My uncle lives in Kaohsiung.
column9: More formal than 伯伯. It is also a respectful way to talk about or address an older man who is a friend of your father: 李伯父. The wife is 伯母.

column3: It is also a polite way to address a friend's mother, or any woman about the age of your own mother: 伯母好. The partner of 伯父. 母 is a form of 女 with dots added to tell the two apart.
column6: Bómǔ zuò de cài hěn hǎochī.
column7: My aunt's cooking is delicious.
column9: It is also a polite way to address a friend's mother, or any woman about the age of your own mother: 伯母好. The partner of 伯父. 母 is a form of 女 with dots added to tell the two apart.

column3: Mostly met in 叔叔 and 叔父. Children also call any man about their father's age 叔叔. It is for the father's younger brother, as 伯 is for the elder.
column7: Good morning, Uncle Li.
column9: Mostly met in 叔叔 and 叔父. Children also call any man about their father's age 叔叔. It is for the father's younger brother, as 伯 is for the elder.

column3: Your father's sister. 姑妈 is also said for her, and an older sister of your father may be called 大姑.
column7: My aunt is very fond of children.
column9: Your father's sister. 姑媽 is also said for her, and an older sister of your father may be called 大姑.

column3: It works as an adjective and as a verb, for someone who gets shy in front of others: 他很害羞, 别害羞, 她害羞地笑了.
column4: 他在人多的时候很害羞。
column5: 他在人多的時候很害羞。
column6: Tā zài rén duō de shíhou hěn hàixiū.
column7: He is very shy when there are many people.
column9: It works as an adjective and as a verb, for someone who gets shy in front of others: 他很害羞, 別害羞, 她害羞地笑了.

column3: It means working as a teacher, and it is a verb with its object, so the pieces can come apart: 他教了十年书. To teach a subject or a person, use 教 alone: 教英文, 教学生.
column7: She teaches at an elementary school.
column9: It means working as a teacher, and it is a verb with its object, so the pieces can come apart: 他教了十年書. To teach a subject or a person, use 教 alone: 教英文, 教學生.

column3: A way of doing something, often of a person's action: 这种作法不好. 做法 means the same; on the mainland it is the usual spelling, and Taiwan uses both.
column6: Tā de zuòfǎ bù tài hǎo.
column7: His way of doing it is not very good.
column9: A way of doing something, often of a person's action: 這種作法不好. 做法 means the same; on the mainland it is the usual spelling, and Taiwan uses both.

column3: It does not stand alone in everyday speech; it turns up in 例子, 例如, 举例 and 比例. In writing, 以……为例 is a common frame meaning "take ... as an example".
column6: Wǒmen yǐ zhè ge cí wéi lì.
column7: Let's take this word as an example.
column9: It does not stand alone in everyday speech; it turns up in 例子, 例如, 舉例 and 比例. In writing, 以……為例 is a common frame meaning "take ... as an example".

column3: A common spoken word for studying and being a student: 他在台北念书. 读书 means the same. Like other verb-object words it can be split: 念了很多书. For reading aloud, 念 alone is used.
column7: He is studying in Taipei.
column9: A common spoken word for studying and being a student: 他在台北念書. 讀書 means the same. Like other verb-object words it can be split: 念了很多書. For reading aloud, 念 alone is used.

column3: 学 ends the names of fields of study: 数学, 化学, 文学, 医学. 数学课 is the class and 数学老师 the teacher. In 数学 the character is read shù, "number", but as the verb "to count" it is read shǔ.
column6: Wǒ de shùxué bù tài hǎo.
column7: I am not very good at math.
column9: 學 ends the names of fields of study: 數學, 化學, 文學, 醫學. 數學課 is the class and 數學老師 the teacher. In 數學 the character is read shù, "number", but as the verb "to count" it is read shǔ.

column3: The word for grammar in Taiwan: a grammar point is 文法重点. The mainland more often says 语法, which people in Taiwan understand too.
column6: Zhōngwén de wénfǎ bù tài nán.
column7: Chinese grammar is not too difficult.
column9: The word for grammar in Taiwan: a grammar point is 文法重點. The mainland more often says 語法, which people in Taiwan understand too.

column3: You mostly meet it in 除了……以外, "besides" or "except". With 也 or 还 it adds something ("besides Chinese, he also speaks Japanese"), and with 都 or 没 it leaves something out. In arithmetic 除以 is "divided by": 十除以二.
column6: Shí chú yǐ èr děngyú wǔ.
column7: Ten divided by two is five.
column9: You mostly meet it in 除了……以外, "besides" or "except". With 也 or 還 it adds something ("besides Chinese, he also speaks Japanese"), and with 都 or 沒 it leaves something out. In arithmetic 除以 is "divided by": 十除以二.

column3: Taiwan's short word for elementary school, from 国民小学: 他在念国小. The school levels are 国小, 国中 (junior high) and 高中 (senior high). The mainland says 小学, which Taiwan uses too.
column7: His younger brother is in elementary school.
column9: Taiwan's short word for elementary school, from 國民小學: 他在念國小. The school levels are 國小, 國中 (junior high) and 高中 (senior high). The mainland says 小學, which Taiwan uses too.

column3: The school break in early April, which in Taiwan runs together with the Tomb Sweeping holiday. Other breaks are named the same way: 暑假 and 寒假.
column7: We are going to Taitung for spring break.
column9: The school break in early April, which in Taiwan runs together with the Tomb Sweeping holiday. Other breaks are named the same way: 暑假 and 寒假.

column3: It is the "vacation" in 放假 (to get time off), 请假 (ask for leave), 暑假, 寒假 and 假日.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng qǐng yī tiān jià.
column7: I would like to take a day off.
column9: It is the "vacation" in 放假 (to get time off), 請假 (ask for leave), 暑假, 寒假 and 假日.

column3: -友 names a friend through something you share: 室友 shares your room, 网友 you know online, 球友 plays ball with you. A 室友 can live in your dorm room or in the same rented apartment.
column7: My roommate is Japanese.
column9: -友 names a friend through something you share: 室友 shares your room, 網友 you know online, 球友 plays ball with you. A 室友 can live in your dorm room or in the same rented apartment.

column3: A seat at a table, in a theater or in a restaurant: 有位子吗, 找位子, 让位子. 座位 is the more formal word for the same thing.
column7: Is there a seat here?
column9: A seat at a table, in a theater or in a restaurant: 有位子嗎, 找位子, 讓位子. 座位 is the more formal word for the same thing.

column3: Used of studying hard. It works as an adjective and a verb, and takes 很 or 不太: 他很用功, 不太用功. For a hardworking employee, 认真 or 努力 fit better.
column7: He studies very hard.
column9: Used of studying hard. It works as an adjective and a verb, and takes 很 or 不太: 他很用功, 不太用功. For a hardworking employee, 認真 or 努力 fit better.

column3: A bedroom. 卧室 is the more common word; in speech people often just say 房间, the everyday word for any room. 房 ends many room words: 书房, 厨房, 客房.
column6: Wǒ de wòfáng zài èr lóu.
column7: My bedroom is on the second floor.
column9: A bedroom. 臥室 is the more common word; in speech people often just say 房間, the everyday word for any room. 房 ends many room words: 書房, 廚房, 客房.

column3: The room for bathing, where you 洗澡; it need not hold a toilet, which people call 厕所 or 洗手间. It is also the word for a public bathhouse. 室 names rooms in many words: 教室, 卧室, 办公室.
column7: There is hot water in the bathroom.
column9: The room for bathing, where you 洗澡; it need not hold a toilet, which people call 廁所 or 洗手間. It is also the word for a public bathhouse. 室 names rooms in many words: 教室, 臥室, 辦公室.

column3: The room at home for working and reading, counted with 间: 一间书房. 房 ends many room words: 卧房, 厨房, 客房.
column7: Dad is reading in the study.
column9: The room at home for working and reading, counted with 間: 一間書房. 房 ends many room words: 臥房, 廚房, 客房.

column3: The table where a family eats, counted with 张: 一张餐桌. What is on it takes 上: 餐桌上. 桌子 is the general word for any table or desk, and 饭桌 is the everyday spoken word for the table you eat at.
column6: Cānzhuō shang yǒu sān ge cài.
column7: There are three dishes on the dining table.
column9: The table where a family eats, counted with 張: 一張餐桌. What is on it takes 上: 餐桌上. 桌子 is the general word for any table or desk, and 飯桌 is the everyday spoken word for the table you eat at.

column3: In speech it usually comes with 子, as 柜子, or in names of furniture: 衣柜, 书柜, 鞋柜. 柜台 is a shop counter.
column6: Wǒ bǎ shū fàng zài shū guì lǐ.
column7: I put the books in the bookcase.
column9: In speech it usually comes with 子, as 櫃子, or in names of furniture: 衣櫃, 書櫃, 鞋櫃. 櫃檯 is a shop counter.

column3: The countryside as opposed to the city. 回乡下 is what you say about visiting family who live there, such as grandparents.
column7: My grandmother lives in the countryside.
column9: The countryside as opposed to the city. 回鄉下 is what you say about visiting family who live there, such as grandparents.

column3: In speech it usually comes with 子: 蚊子. It is also in 蚊香 (mosquito coil), 蚊帐 (mosquito net) and 防蚊液 (repellent).
column7: At night you need to light a mosquito coil.
column9: In speech it usually comes with 子: 蚊子. It is also in 蚊香 (mosquito coil), 蚊帳 (mosquito net) and 防蚊液 (repellent).

column3: Being bitten is 被蚊子咬. A mosquito is counted with 只: 一只蚊子. The repellent is 防蚊液.
column7: I got bitten by a mosquito.
column9: Being bitten is 被蚊子咬. A mosquito is counted with 只: 一只蚊子. The repellent is 防蚊液.

column3: A verb with its object, so it can split: 流了很多汗. 出汗 is also said. 满头大汗 means sweat all over the head.
column7: You sweat after exercise.
column9: A verb with its object, so it can split: 流了很多汗. 出汗 is also said. 滿頭大汗 means sweat all over the head.

column3: Counted with 个: 一个枕头. The pillow takes the noun ending 头, while 枕 alone is the verb "to rest one's head on": 枕着手臂睡.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng yào yī ge xīn zhěntou.
column7: I would like a new pillow.
column9: Counted with 個: 一個枕頭. The pillow takes the noun ending 頭, while 枕 alone is the verb "to rest one's head on": 枕著手臂睡.

column3: Slippers worn at home, and also flip-flops or beach sandals. People often take off their shoes at the door and put on slippers: 换拖鞋. Counted with 双: 一双拖鞋.
column7: Please change into slippers when you come in.
column9: Slippers worn at home, and also flip-flops or beach sandals. People often take off their shoes at the door and put on slippers: 換拖鞋. Counted with 雙: 一雙拖鞋.

column3: Counted with 块: 一块肥皂. 香皂 is scented soap for the body and hands, and 洗手液 is liquid hand soap.
column7: You have to wash your hands with soap.
column9: Counted with 塊: 一塊肥皂. 香皂 is scented soap for the body and hands, and 洗手液 is liquid hand soap.

column3: A tube is counted with 条: 一条牙膏. 膏 is any paste or ointment, as in 药膏. 挤牙膏 means squeezing out toothpaste and also, figuratively, giving information only a little at a time.
column6: Zhè tiáo yágāo kuài yòngwán le.
column7: This tube of toothpaste is almost used up.
column9: A tube is counted with 條: 一條牙膏. 膏 is any paste or ointment, as in 藥膏. 擠牙膏 means squeezing out toothpaste and also, figuratively, giving information only a little at a time.

column3: In Taiwan it is the general word for plain paper in a bathroom or on a restaurant table, and facial tissues are 面纸. On the mainland it is toilet paper and tissues are 纸巾.
column7: There is no toilet paper left in the bathroom.
column9: In Taiwan it is the general word for plain paper in a bathroom or on a restaurant table, and facial tissues are 面紙. On the mainland it is toilet paper and tissues are 紙巾.

column3: Mostly met in compounds: 篮子, 菜篮 (shopping basket) and 篮球, where the "basket" is the hoop. 投篮 is to shoot a basket.
column6: Zhuō shang yǒu yī lán shuǐguǒ.
column7: There is a basket of fruit on the table.
column9: Mostly met in compounds: 籃子, 菜籃 (shopping basket) and 籃球, where the "basket" is the hoop. 投籃 is to shoot a basket.

column3: 篮 also works as a measure word: 一篮水果 is a basket of fruit. A basket is counted with 个, and 菜篮子 is a shopping basket.
column6: Lánzi lǐ yǒu hěn duō shuǐguǒ.
column7: There is a lot of fruit in the basket.
column9: 籃 also works as a measure word: 一籃水果 is a basket of fruit. A basket is counted with 個, and 菜籃子 is a shopping basket.

column3: Weekends count as well as public holidays: any day off from work or school. An official public holiday is 国定假日 in Taiwan and 法定假日 on the mainland. It is a noun; to get time off is 放假. For "vacation" 假 is read jià, but for "fake" it is jiǎ.
column6: Jiàrì yèshì de rén hěn duō.
column7: On holidays the night market is crowded.
column9: Weekends count as well as public holidays: any day off from work or school. An official public holiday is 國定假日 in Taiwan and 法定假日 on the mainland. It is a noun; to get time off is 放假. For "vacation" 假 is read jià, but for "fake" it is jiǎ.

column3: A verb for the exercise: 去慢跑 (go jogging), 在公园慢跑. Plain "run" is 跑步.
column4: 我每天早上去公园慢跑。
column5: 我每天早上去公園慢跑。
column6: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang qù gōngyuán mànpǎo.
column7: I go jogging in the park every morning.
column9: A verb for the exercise: 去慢跑 (go jogging), 在公園慢跑. Plain "run" is 跑步.

column3: It is both the noun "picnic" and the verb "to have a picnic": 去野餐, 在公园野餐. The mat for it is a 野餐垫.
column7: Let's go on a picnic on Sunday.
column9: It is both the noun "picnic" and the verb "to have a picnic": 去野餐, 在公園野餐. The mat for it is a 野餐墊.

column3: A spoken verb, used alone, doubled or with 一: 聊聊 and 聊一聊 ("have a chat") sound softer. The topic can follow it: 聊工作. With 天 it makes 聊天.
column7: Let's have a chat.
column9: A spoken verb, used alone, doubled or with 一: 聊聊 and 聊一聊 ("have a chat") sound softer. The topic can follow it: 聊工作. With 天 it makes 聊天.

column3: The verb depends on the instrument: 弹 for strings and keyboards (弹吉他, 弹钢琴), 吹 for winds, 拉 for the violin. 乐 is read yuè for "music" but lè for "happy".
column7: What instrument can you play?
column9: The verb depends on the instrument: 彈 for strings and keyboards (彈吉他, 彈鋼琴), 吹 for winds, 拉 for the violin. 樂 is read yuè for "music" but lè for "happy".

column3: A loanword written with characters that only stand for the sound. The verb is 弹: 弹吉他. A guitarist is 吉他手, and the instrument is counted with 把: 一把吉他.
column7: He can play the guitar.
column9: A loanword written with characters that only stand for the sound. The verb is 彈: 彈吉他. A guitarist is 吉他手, and the instrument is counted with 把: 一把吉他.

column3: A place to sit and drink tea, sometimes with snacks. 馆 names a public place or shop in many words: 餐馆, 图书馆. A quiet, traditional teahouse is also called a 茶艺馆.
column7: We are drinking tea at the teahouse.
column9: A place to sit and drink tea, sometimes with snacks. 館 names a public place or shop in many words: 餐館, 圖書館. A quiet, traditional teahouse is also called a 茶藝館.

column3: The same word as 茶馆 with the 儿 ending, which belongs to Beijing and northern speech. Elsewhere people mostly say 茶馆. Here 儿 is not a syllable of its own but a retroflex ending, so the r is added to the last syllable.
column7: Let's go and sit in the teahouse.
column9: The same word as 茶館 with the 兒 ending, which belongs to Beijing and northern speech. Elsewhere people mostly say 茶館. Here 兒 is not a syllable of its own but a retroflex ending, so the r is added to the last syllable.

column3: A loanword from English, with 派 and 对 chosen for the sound. It is used for lively parties: 开派对, 生日派对. A quieter gathering is more likely to be a 聚会.
column7: We are having a party this weekend.
column9: A loanword from English, with 派 and 對 chosen for the sound. It is used for lively parties: 開派對, 生日派對. A quieter gathering is more likely to be a 聚會.

column3: Three senses: a piece, 一块蛋糕; "one yuan" in speech, 一块钱 (one NT dollar in Taiwan); and "together", 一块去, a spoken way to say 一起. 块 is the measure word for pieces, lumps and coins.
column7: I ate a piece of cake.
column9: Three senses: a piece, 一塊蛋糕; "one yuan" in speech, 一塊錢 (one NT dollar in Taiwan); and "together", 一塊去, a spoken way to say 一起. 塊 is the measure word for pieces, lumps and coins.

column3: Both jet lag and the plain difference between two places: 有时差, 台湾和日本有一个小时的时差. To get over jet lag, people in Taiwan say 调时差, and on the mainland 倒时差. Here 差 is read chā, "difference". The reading chà, "to fall short", is the mainland's; Taiwan reads 差 as chā throughout.
column4: 台湾和日本只有一个小时的时差。
column5: 台灣和日本只有一個小時的時差。
column6: Táiwān hé Rìběn zhǐyǒu yī ge xiǎoshí de shíchā.
column7: Taiwan and Japan are only one hour apart.
column9: Both jet lag and the plain difference between two places: 有時差, 臺灣和日本有一個小時的時差. To get over jet lag, people in Taiwan say 調時差, and on the mainland 倒時差. Here 差 is read chā, "difference". The reading chà, "to fall short", is the mainland's; Taiwan reads 差 as chā throughout.

column3: The verb for going to one is 泡, "soak": 泡温泉. The word names both the spring water and the bathing place built around it.
column6: Dōngtiān qù pào wēnquán hěn shūfu.
column7: Soaking in a hot spring in winter is very comfortable.
column9: The verb for going to one is 泡, "soak": 泡溫泉. The word names both the spring water and the bathing place built around it.

column3: On the mainland it covers every kind. In Taiwan the everyday word for scooters and motorcycles alike is 机车 (a big one is a 重机); 摩托车 is understood but sounds more formal. You ride it with 骑. 摩托 is a loanword for "motor".
column7: He rides a motorcycle to work.
column9: On the mainland it covers every kind. In Taiwan the everyday word for scooters and motorcycles alike is 機車 (a big one is a 重機); 摩托車 is understood but sounds more formal. You ride it with 騎. 摩托 is a loanword for "motor".

column3: In Taiwan the everyday word for a scooter: 骑机车. On the mainland 机车 is a railway locomotive, and a scooter is 摩托车. Taiwan slang also uses it for a fussy, annoying person: 你很机车.
column6: Zài Táiwān hěn duō rén qí jīchē.
column7: Many people in Taiwan ride scooters.
column9: In Taiwan the everyday word for a scooter: 騎機車. On the mainland 機車 is a railway locomotive, and a scooter is 摩托車. Taiwan slang also uses it for a fussy, annoying person: 你很機車.

column3: The metro of Taipei, Kaohsiung and other Taiwan cities; on the mainland it is 地铁. You take it with 坐 or 搭: 搭捷运, and the station is 捷运站.
column7: I take the MRT to work every day.
column9: The metro of Taipei, Kaohsiung and other Taiwan cities; on the mainland it is 地鐵. You take it with 坐 or 搭: 搭捷運, and the station is 捷運站.

column3: The usual verb for taking a vehicle in Taiwan: 搭捷运, 搭公车, 搭飞机. The mainland more often says 坐, which Taiwan uses too. It also means to put up (搭帐篷, pitch a tent), to match (搭配) and, with a person, to go along: 搭便车, catch a ride.
column4: 我们明天搭飞机去台北。
column5: 我們明天搭飛機去台北。
column6: Wǒmen míngtiān dā fēijī qù Táiběi.
column7: We are taking a plane to Taipei tomorrow.
column9: The usual verb for taking a vehicle in Taiwan: 搭捷運, 搭公車, 搭飛機. The mainland more often says 坐, which Taiwan uses too. It also means to put up (搭帳篷, pitch a tent), to match (搭配) and, with a person, to go along: 搭便車, catch a ride.

column3: Continents are named with 洲: 亚洲, 欧洲, 美洲. 非 alone can stand for Africa, but it also means "not".
column6: Tā míngnián yào qù Fēizhōu lǚxíng.
column7: He is going to travel to Africa next year.
column9: Continents are named with 洲: 亞洲, 歐洲, 美洲. 非 alone can stand for Africa, but it also means "not".

column3: The Americas, North and South together: 北美洲 and 南美洲. 美国 is only the United States. In compounds, 美 can be short for either 美洲 or 美国.
column7: There are many countries in the Americas.
column9: The Americas, North and South together: 北美洲 and 南美洲. 美國 is only the United States. In compounds, 美 can be short for either 美洲 or 美國.

column3: People are 欧洲人. In compounds, 欧 is short for Europe, for the European Union in 欧盟 and for the euro in 欧元.
column6: Shǔjià wǒ xiǎng qù Ōuzhōu wán.
column7: I want to go to Europe over the summer vacation.
column9: People are 歐洲人. In compounds, 歐 is short for Europe, for the European Union in 歐盟 and for the euro in 歐元.

column3: Asians are 亚洲人, and the regions are 东亚 and 东南亚 (Southeast Asia). In Taiwan 亚 is read Yǎ.
column7: Taiwan is in Asia.
column9: Asians are 亞洲人, and the regions are 東亞 and 東南亞 (Southeast Asia). In Taiwan 亞 is read Yǎ.

column3: Counted with 把: 一把钥匙, and a car key is 车钥匙. A key on a keyboard is 键 instead. 匙 is read shi in this word, but chí when it means a spoon.
column7: I forgot to bring my key.
column9: Counted with 把: 一把鑰匙, and a car key is 車鑰匙. A key on a keyboard is 鍵 instead. 匙 is read shi in this word, but chí when it means a spoon.

column3: Only found inside words such as 脖子. The written word for the neck is 颈, as in 颈部.
column6: Tā de bó zi hěn cháng.
column7: He has a long neck.
column9: Only found inside words such as 脖子. The written word for the neck is 頸, as in 頸部.

column3: The everyday word for the neck; 颈 is the written one (颈部). A sore neck is 脖子痛, and a scarf, 围巾, goes around it.
column7: My neck hurts a lot.
column9: The everyday word for the neck; 頸 is the written one (頸部). A sore neck is 脖子痛, and a scarf, 圍巾, goes around it.

column3: You call one with 叫救护车. The emergency number is 119 in Taiwan and 120 on the mainland; the police are 110 on both sides.
column7: Quick, call an ambulance!
column9: You call one with 叫救護車. The emergency number is 119 in Taiwan and 120 on the mainland; the police are 110 on both sides.

column3: Both the verb and the cough itself: 他一直咳嗽, and 咳嗽药 is cough medicine. It often comes with a cold: 感冒咳嗽.
column7: I keep coughing.
column9: Both the verb and the cough itself: 他一直咳嗽, and 咳嗽藥 is cough medicine. It often comes with a cold: 感冒咳嗽.

column3: Also figurative, for a problem that is a headache to deal with: 这件事让人头痛. For other body parts the same 痛 works: 牙痛, 肚子痛.
column6: Wǒ tóutòng, xiǎng huí jiā xiūxi.
column7: I have a headache and want to go home and rest.
column9: Also figurative, for a problem that is a headache to deal with: 這件事讓人頭痛. For other body parts the same 痛 works: 牙痛, 肚子痛.

column3: Two uses: to register at a hospital or clinic to get a number, 先挂号再看医生, and to send a registered letter, 挂号信. Many clinics let you do it online.
column6: Wǒ yào xiān guàhào zài kàn yīshēng.
column7: I have to register first before seeing the doctor.
column9: Two uses: to register at a hospital or clinic to get a number, 先掛號再看醫生, and to send a registered letter, 掛號信. Many clinics let you do it online.

column3: The shop where you buy medicine. In Taiwan 药局 is just as common, and a 药妆店 is a drugstore that also sells makeup; the mainland usually says 药店.
column7: The pharmacy is next to the hospital.
column9: The shop where you buy medicine. In Taiwan 藥局 is just as common, and a 藥妝店 is a drugstore that also sells makeup; the mainland usually says 藥店.

column3: A verb with its object, so it can split: 救了我一命 "saved my life". As a shout it is for real danger; for everyday help say 帮帮我 or 请问.
column7: Help! Someone is hurt!
column9: A verb with its object, so it can split: 救了我一命 "saved my life". As a shout it is for real danger; for everyday help say 幫幫我 or 請問.

column3: It works like a verb, so 没钱 negates it and 很 can stand in front: 他很有钱. 有钱人 is a rich person. It is a plain statement, but can sound envious or ironic.
column7: His family is very rich.
column9: It works like a verb, so 沒錢 negates it and 很 can stand in front: 他很有錢. 有錢人 is a rich person. It is a plain statement, but can sound envious or ironic.

column3: The boss's wife, or the woman who runs a small shop, market stall or restaurant herself. Customers use it to address her too, and her husband is 老板.
column7: The shop owner is very nice.
column9: The boss's wife, or the woman who runs a small shop, market stall or restaurant herself. Customers use it to address her too, and her husband is 老板.

column3: 员 ends many words for people with a job or in a group: 店员, 服务员, 职员, 公务员.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn de diànyuán hěn qīnqiè.
column7: The clerks in this shop are very friendly.
column9: 員 ends many words for people with a job or in a group: 店員, 服務員, 職員, 公務員.

column3: Reserving a seat: a restaurant table, or a seat on a train or plane. 订 is the verb and 位 the object, so they split: 订好位了, 订了两个位. 订票 is booking the ticket itself.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng dìngwèi, liǎng ge rén.
column7: I would like to make a reservation for two.
column9: Reserving a seat: a restaurant table, or a seat on a train or plane. 訂 is the verb and 位 the object, so they split: 訂好位了, 訂了兩個位. 訂票 is booking the ticket itself.

column3: Often shortened to 百货. A department store everywhere; a mall is a 商场 or 购物中心. The food floor is the 美食街 in Taiwan and the 美食广场 on the mainland.
column7: What time does the department store open?
column9: Often shortened to 百貨. A department store everywhere; a mall is a 商場 or 購物中心. The food floor is the 美食街 in Taiwan and the 美食廣場 on the mainland.

column3: The verb for going is 逛: 逛夜市 means to wander among the stalls, not only to eat. The food is 小吃, small snacks.
column4: 我们晚上去夜市吃小吃。
column5: 我們晚上去夜市吃小吃。
column6: Wǒmen wǎnshang qù yèshì chī xiǎochī.
column7: This evening we are going to the night market to eat snacks.
column9: The verb for going is 逛: 逛夜市 means to wander among the stalls, not only to eat. The food is 小吃, small snacks.

column3: To stroll around the shops, with no need to buy: 去逛街, 逛了一下午的街. A verb with its object, so it can split.
column6: Zhōumò wǒ cháng hé péngyou guàngjiē.
column7: On weekends I often go shopping with friends.
column9: To stroll around the shops, with no need to buy: 去逛街, 逛了一下午的街. A verb with its object, so it can split.

column3: The sign on the door of a restaurant, hotel or theater: no seats left. In speech, 今天客满了 or just 满了.
column7: The restaurant is full today.
column9: The sign on the door of a restaurant, hotel or theater: no seats left. In speech, 今天客滿了 or just 滿了.

column3: Used for paying by card: 可以刷卡吗？ In Taiwan small stalls and night markets often take cash only, so it is worth asking; on the mainland stalls mostly take phone payment, 扫码.
column7: Can I pay by card here?
column9: Used for paying by card: 可以刷卡嗎？ In Taiwan small stalls and night markets often take cash only, so it is worth asking; on the mainland stalls mostly take phone payment, 掃碼.

column3: Raincoat, 雨 "rain" + 衣 "clothes". You put one on with 穿: 穿雨衣, and count it with 件: 一件雨衣. Other things for the rain: 雨伞 "umbrella", 雨鞋 "rain boots".
column7: It is raining; please wear a raincoat.
column9: Raincoat, 雨 "rain" + 衣 "clothes". You put one on with 穿: 穿雨衣, and count it with 件: 一件雨衣. Other things for the rain: 雨傘 "umbrella", 雨鞋 "rain boots".

column3: Underwear in general, such as bras and undershirts; 内裤 is underpants. It pairs with 外衣, outer clothing: 内 inside, 外 outside.
column4: 我在百货公司买了内衣。
column5: 我在百貨公司買了內衣。
column6: Wǒ zài bǎihuògōngsī mǎi le nèiyī.
column7: I bought underwear at the department store.
column9: Underwear in general, such as bras and undershirts; 內褲 is underpants. It pairs with 外衣, outer clothing: 內 inside, 外 outside.

column3: A tip, extra money for service: 小 "small" + 费 "fee". Tipping is not the custom in Taiwan, and many restaurants add a service charge of 10% (服务费) instead. So 不用给小费 "no need to tip". 给小费 is the verb phrase.
column6: Zài Táiwān bù yòng gěi xiǎofèi.
column7: You don't need to tip in Taiwan.
column9: A tip, extra money for service: 小 "small" + 費 "fee". Tipping is not the custom in Taiwan, and many restaurants add a service charge of 10% (服務費) instead. So 不用給小費 "no need to tip". 給小費 is the verb phrase.

column3: The loose coins and small bills you carry: 找零钱 is to give change, and 没有零钱 means you have nothing small. 零 means odd bits here, as in 零食 "snacks". A 零钱包 is a coin purse.
column7: I have no small change on me.
column9: The loose coins and small bills you carry: 找零錢 is to give change, and 沒有零錢 means you have nothing small. 零 means odd bits here, as in 零食 "snacks". A 零錢包 is a coin purse.

column3: Money for small expenses, usually given by parents to a child: 给零用钱. Adults also use it for money kept aside for little spending. On the mainland 零花钱 is just as common.
column4: 爸爸每个星期给我零用钱。
column5: 爸爸每個星期給我零用錢。
column6: Bàba měi ge xīngqī gěi wǒ língyòngqián.
column7: Dad gives me pocket money every week.
column9: Money for small expenses, usually given by parents to a child: 給零用錢. Adults also use it for money kept aside for little spending. On the mainland 零花錢 is just as common.

column3: A loanword from the English sound. 水果沙拉 is fruit salad and 沙拉酱 is the dressing. Order with 一份沙拉 or 一盘沙拉.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng diǎn yī fèn shālā.
column7: I would like to order a salad.
column9: A loanword from the English sound. 水果沙拉 is fruit salad and 沙拉醬 is the dressing. Order with 一份沙拉 or 一盤沙拉.

column3: The waiter asks how done you want it with 几分熟: 三分熟 is rare, 五分熟 medium and 全熟 well done. 排 names other cuts too: 猪排 is a pork chop and 鸡排 a fried chicken cutlet.
column6: Nǐ de niúpái yào jǐ fēn shú?
column7: How would you like your steak done?
column9: The waiter asks how done you want it with 幾分熟: 三分熟 is rare, 五分熟 medium and 全熟 well done. 排 names other cuts too: 豬排 is a pork chop and 雞排 a fried chicken cutlet.

column3: A word-for-word translation of the English, so it is not a dog at all. Counted with 根: 一根热狗. Convenience stores and night markets sell them.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng chī yī gēn règǒu.
column7: I want to eat a hot dog.
column9: A word-for-word translation of the English, so it is not a dog at all. Counted with 根: 一根熱狗. Convenience stores and night markets sell them.

column3: A plain steamed bun with no filling, often eaten at breakfast with 豆浆. A bun with a meat or vegetable filling is a 包子. 头 here is just a noun suffix.
column6: Tā zǎocān chī mántou hé dòujiāng.
column7: He has a steamed bun and soy milk for breakfast.
column9: A plain steamed bun with no filling, often eaten at breakfast with 豆漿. A bun with a meat or vegetable filling is a 包子. 頭 here is just a noun suffix.

column3: Only found inside words: 橘子 is a tangerine or mandarin. The color orange is 橘色 in Taiwan and mostly 橙色 on the mainland.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng chī yī ge jú zi.
column7: I want to eat a tangerine.
column9: Only found inside words: 橘子 is a tangerine or mandarin. The color orange is 橘色 in Taiwan and mostly 橙色 on the mainland.

column3: Tangerine, mandarin orange, the small loose-skinned fruit: 剥橘子 "peel a tangerine". The larger orange is called 柳丁 in Taiwan, while the mainland says 橙子. Counted by weight with 斤 or with 个. 子 is neutral.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le yī jīn júzi.
column7: I bought a catty of tangerines.
column9: Tangerine, mandarin orange, the small loose-skinned fruit: 剝橘子 "peel a tangerine". The larger orange is called 柳丁 in Taiwan, while the mainland says 橙子. Counted by weight with 斤 or with 個. 子 is neutral.

column3: 果 ends many fruit names, such as 苹果. 芒果冰, shaved ice with mango, is a well-known summer treat in Taiwan, and 芒果干 is dried mango.
column7: Taiwan's mangoes are delicious.
column9: 果 ends many fruit names, such as 苹果. 芒果冰, shaved ice with mango, is a well-known summer treat in Taiwan, and 芒果干 is dried mango.

column3: 冻顶乌龙, from Taiwan, is a well-known kind. 乌龙 alone also means an embarrassing mix-up, and 乌龙球 is an own goal in soccer. 乌 began as a picture of a bird, and its meaning "black" extends from "crow": black as a crow.
column7: I like to drink oolong tea.
column9: 凍頂烏龍, from Taiwan, is a well-known kind. 烏龍 alone also means an embarrassing mix-up, and 烏龍球 is an own goal in soccer. 烏 began as a picture of a bird, and its meaning "black" extends from "crow": black as a crow.

column3: A classic breakfast is 豆浆 with 烧饼 or 油条. It comes 甜 (sweet), 无糖 (unsweetened) or 咸 (salty). Counted with 杯 or 碗: 一碗豆浆.
column6: Wǒ zǎoshang hē yī bēi dòujiāng.
column7: I drink a cup of soy milk in the morning.
column9: A classic breakfast is 豆漿 with 燒餅 or 油條. It comes 甜 (sweet), 無糖 (unsweetened) or 鹹 (salty). Counted with 杯 or 碗: 一碗豆漿.

column3: Ordering a drink: 加冰块 adds ice, 去冰 means no ice and 少冰 less ice. 块 is also the measure word for lumps: 一块冰.
column7: Please don't put any ice in.
column9: Ordering a drink: 加冰塊 adds ice, 去冰 means no ice and 少冰 less ice. 塊 is also the measure word for lumps: 一塊冰.

column3: The word on café menus for cakes, tarts and puddings, eaten after a meal or with tea: 点甜点. 点心 is broader and can be savory.
column4: 吃完饭以后，我想吃甜点。
column5: 吃完飯以後，我想吃甜點。
column6: Chī wán fàn yǐhòu, wǒ xiǎng chī tiándiǎn.
column7: After the meal I would like to have dessert.
column9: The word on café menus for cakes, tarts and puddings, eaten after a meal or with tea: 點甜點. 點心 is broader and can be savory.

column3: Mostly in 味道 "flavor" and 口味 "taste", and in 香味 and 臭味 "bad smell". It is also a suffix for a feel or quality, as in 人情味 "human touch".
column6: Zhè dào cài de wèi dào hěn hǎo.
column7: This dish tastes very good.
column9: Mostly in 味道 "flavor" and 口味 "taste", and in 香味 and 臭味 "bad smell". It is also a suffix for a feel or quality, as in 人情味 "human touch".

column3: A can, jar or tin and also the measure word for them: 一罐可乐, 两罐牛奶. 罐头 is canned food and 罐子 a jar.
column6: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng guàn kělè.
column7: I bought two cans of cola.
column9: A can, jar or tin and also the measure word for them: 一罐可樂, 兩罐牛奶. 罐頭 is canned food and 罐子 a jar.

column3: The standard cooking method for most home dishes: 炒饭, 炒面, 炒青菜. It also means to speculate (炒股票) and, in 炒鱿鱼, to fire someone.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng chǎo yī ge qīngcài.
column7: I want to stir-fry a vegetable dish.
column9: The standard cooking method for most home dishes: 炒飯, 炒麵, 炒青菜. It also means to speculate (炒股票) and, in 炒魷魚, to fire someone.

column3: For deep-frying in oil, as in 炸鸡 and 炸薯条; stir-frying in a pan is 炒.
column7: Mom is frying fish in the kitchen.
column9: For deep-frying in oil, as in 炸雞 and 炸薯條; stir-frying in a pan is 炒.

column3: Two uses. After a list it means "and so on": 苹果、香蕉等等. As a request, 等等！ is "wait a moment!", the same as 等一下, and it is spoken.
column4: 桌子上有苹果、香蕉、橘子等等。
column5: 桌子上有蘋果、香蕉、橘子等等。
column6: Zhuōzi shang yǒu píngguǒ, xiāngjiāo, júzi děngděng.
column7: On the table there are apples, bananas, tangerines and so on.
column9: Two uses. After a list it means "and so on": 苹果、香蕉等等. As a request, 等等！ is "wait a moment!", the same as 等一下, and it is spoken.

column3: Two uses: a modest "not bad" in answer to 你好吗？, and "luckily": 还好你来了. It is milder than 很好 and shows little feeling. 还 is hái here, but huán when it means to pay back or return.
column7: Luckily you came.
column9: Two uses: a modest "not bad" in answer to 你好嗎？, and "luckily": 還好你來了. It is milder than 很好 and shows little feeling. 還 is hái here, but huán when it means to pay back or return.

column3: Used for timing and amount: 刚好十点 "exactly ten o'clock", 刚好够 "just enough". 刚 also appears in 刚才 "a moment ago".
column4: 我到的时候，车刚好来了。
column5: 我到的時候，車剛好來了。
column6: Wǒ dào de shíhou, chē gānghǎo lái le.
column7: When I got there, the bus happened to arrive just then.
column9: Used for timing and amount: 剛好十點 "exactly ten o'clock", 剛好夠 "just enough". 剛 also appears in 剛才 "a moment ago".

column3: A spoken exclamation of surprise or awe: 哇，好漂亮！ It is not for formal writing.
column7: Wow, it is so big!
column9: A spoken exclamation of surprise or awe: 哇，好漂亮！ It is not for formal writing.

column3: Written style when alone, as on notices: 需预约 "by appointment only". In speech it is 需要, and there is 需求 "demand".
column6: Zhè ge huódòng xū tíqián bàomíng.
column7: You need to sign up in advance for this event.
column9: Written style when alone, as on notices: 需預約 "by appointment only". In speech it is 需要, and there is 需求 "demand".

column3: Must in notices and set words: 必须, 无须 "no need", 须知 "notice to readers". Spoken language uses 要 or 得 instead; 必须 is firmer than both.
column7: Take off your shoes when you go in.
column9: Must in notices and set words: 必須, 無須 "no need", 須知 "notice to readers". Spoken language uses 要 or 得 instead; 必須 is firmer than both.

column3: To soak or steep in liquid: 泡茶, 泡面 "instant noodles", 泡澡, 泡温泉. It is also "bubble": 泡沫 "foam".
column6: Wǒ xiǎng pào yī bēi chá.
column7: I would like to make a cup of tea.
column9: To soak or steep in liquid: 泡茶, 泡麵 "instant noodles", 泡澡, 泡溫泉. It is also "bubble": 泡沫 "foam".

column3: Written style for "and also": 好吃，且便宜. Speech uses 而且 instead, and 且 shows up in 暂且 "for the time being" and 并且 "and also".
column6: Zhèlǐ de cài hǎochī qiě piányi.
column7: The food here is tasty and cheap.
column9: Written style for "and also": 好吃，且便宜. Speech uses 而且 instead, and 且 shows up in 暫且 "for the time being" and 並且 "and also".

column3: A spoken way to bring in an example: 我喜欢运动，比方说游泳。 It is more casual than 例如; 比如(说) is the most common choice in speech.
column4: 我喜欢运动，比方说游泳和跑步。
column5: 我喜歡運動，比方說游泳和跑步。
column6: Wǒ xǐhuan yùndòng, bǐfangshuō yóuyǒng hé pǎobù.
column7: I like sports, for example swimming and running.
column9: A spoken way to bring in an example: 我喜歡運動，比方說游泳。 It is more casual than 例如; 比如(說) is the most common choice in speech.

column3: It goes before a number and measure word (另一个 "another one", 另两个) or before a verb (另有 "there is also", 另买一个). It points to a different thing, not more of the same; 另外 is "besides".
column6: Lìng yī ge rén yě lái le.
column7: Another person came too.
column9: It goes before a number and measure word (另一個 "another one", 另兩個) or before a verb (另有 "there is also", 另買一個). It points to a different thing, not more of the same; 另外 is "besides".

column3: Mostly in 一样 "the same", 这样 "like this", 怎么样 "how is it" and 样子 "appearance". It also counts kinds of things: 三样菜.
column6: Wǒmen diǎn le sān yàng cài.
column7: We ordered three dishes.
column9: Mostly in 一樣 "the same", 這樣 "like this", 怎麼樣 "how is it" and 樣子 "appearance". It also counts kinds of things: 三樣菜.
